title: Meta may use sweeping new commercial TOS to avoid millions in AI licensing fees
abstract: Legal experts are sounding alarms that Meta will soon update its commercial terms to require business accounts to allow Meta to train AI on their linked website content, not just their social media posts. Kicking in on October 30, the TOS update won’t allow businesses to opt out, instead suggesting that businesses stop using Meta services if they won’t agree to let Meta bots freely crawl their linked content. As Nieman Lab reported Thursday, this will affect all business accounts but is particularly shocking for news publishers who could perhaps charge Meta millions in licensing fees to continually access their articles for AI training. Currently news organizations are fighting a battle with OpenAI over whether such training without licensing is fair use, and Meta’s terms seemingly risk granting it sweeping permissions, no matter which way the court leans. “While journalism isn’t the only industry that will be affected by this update, virtually every news organization has at least one Meta business account, including Nieman Lab,” the lab said. Specifically, the updated terms say: You authorize us (or any entity acting on our behalf) to use automated software (such as web scrapers, bots, robots, spiders, crawlers, and user agents) and create test credentials to access, index, cache, analyze, collect, retrieve, or crawl the domains, web pages, or URLs (and any content available through them) that are associated with your products or services, or that are made available through your or users’ use of Meta Company Products and services, and to periodically pull updates from such domains, web pages, or URLs. Meta may use any content from such domains, web pages, or URLs to provide, develop, improve, research, train, and maintain the integrity of, the Meta Company Products, services, and features provided under these Commercial Terms and any other applicable supplemental terms. Notably, there is no mention of AI, but it’s inferred from a single use of the word “train” and references to automated scraping and crawling.

title: Super Scam Me documentary shows what it takes to catch a romance scammer
abstract: If you got a DM from an unverified Jon Bon Jovi account after commenting on one of his official Instagram posts, what would it take to make you believe it was really the rock star hoping to connect? And at what point when he starts asking you to send money—like lose-your-house kind of money—would you snap out of the fantasy and stop draining your bank account? In a documentary premiering Saturday— Super Scam Me —investigative journalist Mariana van Zeller goes deep into this toxic love-bombing terrain. In a clip that Ars is exclusively debuting below, you can see how van Zeller worked with an ethical hacker, Arman the Cyber, to use a fake bitcoin receipt and bait the fake Bon Jovi, giving the victim some much-needed closure. Broadcasting on National Geographic at 9 pm ET and available to stream on Disney+ and Hulu, the documentary takes viewers on an empathetic quest to understand how the line between “lover” and “fraud victim” gets blurred in romance scams that the Federal Trade Commission says cost Americans nearly $1.5 billion in losses each year.

title: Monthly Roundup #47: October 2026
abstract: AI might not yet be eating the physical world. AI is still eating the world of news, and I am finding less and less opportunity to post about other things. My backlog of items grows across most of my secondary topics and I haven’t had time for any side projects. The monthly, no matter what, is sacred. We continue. The story of our time, told once again: Americans are abandoning quite a lot of formerly popular activities, especially hosting at home, as Derek Thompson discussed. Phones and other electronics are in, most things that are not phones are out, with notably rare exceptions. That last line rules everything around us. And we all spend more time at home, which then exploded during Covid and mostly did not recover afterward. Derek does discuss the last two lines later on. You can view exercise classes as an adaptation in four ways: To a lack of other physical activity, to a lack of social activity, to a lack of motivation, and as a wealth effect. Regular people can afford this, and it is a safe way to get things they now lack. Then there are the concerts. This one is what some call a Narrative Violation. We have this collective story about how in the good old days, like the 1960s, people went to all these great cheap concerts, that was part of the good life, and we’ve gotten away from that. But actually they’re making a quiet comeback despite people getting older and all the competition, and also they are great. On the flip side, they are also ‘free’ actions, in that you don’t have to overcome any social barrier. You can buy a ticket. Whereas hosting is, as Derek says, a lot of work to set up, often not fun work. If you’re both working, and children now require vastly more time investment because our society went insane there, who has the time and energy to earn the payoff? Parties also require (and help create and maintain) friends, and creating and maintaining those friends takes even more time. Meanwhile, being alone at home is no longer boring. Being alone at home is great, in the short term. Derek Thompson : Machines in the last half century have accomplished something stranger. They have made other people less necessary to our leisure. Every generation has acquired better ways to entertain itself without leaving the house. The result is a peculiar triumph of modern abundance: We have built a world in which being alone has never been easier, more comfortable, or more fun. And then we wonder why everybody stopped coming over. … Is this what we want? At the risk of invoking Clintonian levels of abstruseness , it depends on what “want” means. Everybody might prefer, in the abstract, a world of dinner parties, neighborhood friendships, and spontaneous gatherings. But on any given Wednesday at 7:45pm., it is easier to look at a screen than to host a party; easier to listen to a podcast while doing yoga than to plan a gathering. This is not so much an individual failure as a coordination failure. There is some coordination failure, but I think this is the wrong central diagnosis. Coordination failure can be overcome, and given the will to do the thing the logistics are far easier today with all our social and communication and logistical tools. The bigger problem is hyperbolic discounting in the face of the new alternatives. In order to get the returns from social activity, you have to invest energy and effort now, and also endure some mild social awkwardness and delay gratification and tolerate some boredom now, and often do things for someone else, in order to build up your friendship and other networks and get into regular habits. I’m also guilty of this trap. I don’t socialize enough. I don’t host enough, and I don’t visit enough. I realize this. But it’s tough. There’s too much to do, both for work and for play. In my case I like to think I have a good excuse, but it is still a mistake. Institute for Family Studies reports at length on America’s demoralized and lost men . Their central presentation is not that young men have, as Senator Hawley put it, ‘no vision for what it is to be a man,’ or that their vision would be bad and captured by toxic influences. It’s that they do have such a positive vision, and it would be good but they despair of living up to it and do not see a path to getting there. We no longer lay out a simple ‘success sequence’ style strategy where you play by the rules and it does not work even for those without problems, and many have problems. The men are culturally told that, by default, they are worthless and unwanted. Or is that the real story? There are some strange sets of beliefs reported. 42% think they are failures and 60% feel they have little control. 72% say who you know is more important than hard work, and 49% saying ‘no matter how hard I work, people like me will never achieve the American dream.’ But 84% say they are at least somewhat ambitious and 81% say they can ‘do just about anything I really set my mind to,’ 75% say their opportunities in life will be greater than their parents, and 82% say they have more potential to succeed than people think. This seems like a lot of very strong framing effects combined with the Revolution of Rising Expectations . The men believe all these things at the same time, in different ways, and you can ‘activate different personas.’ Connections can beat hard work and the deck is stacked against you, but hard work is valid, and if you want it enough and keep your head on straight and resist temptation and despair you can still succeed. But do you want it enough? Can you keep your head on straight and resist temptation and despair? And can you keep searching for an unknown, rather than for a known, so long as the ultimate odds have not changed so much? Another way of looking at this is that if you succeed, there was some way in which you got lucky or did something extraordinary. Something individually atypical is part of every typical success story, even more so than in the past. But if you keep pushing, and try to make your own luck, you will probably eventually get lucky. There are charts and statistics about the usual suspects, like unemployment, depression, disabilities, games, social media, atomization, gambling and pornography. Social media is not like the others, where ‘once a day’ is considered infrequent. Over half of young men feel lonely ‘at least some of the time’ but it is kind of weird not to, isn’t it? The right rate of feeling lonely, like many bad things, is not zero. The report has many other interesting charts. It would be cool to see time lapses. Mostly I came away from this report feeling better rather than worse, if you don’t think AI will upend everything. Ways exist to be found, at least for now. Remember that throughout history, a huge percentage of men failed to have children. It is not a new situation for men to be tested and have to find a way to prove themselves. Broadly my current perspective is the men as a group have never been okay. The difference is that we used to sort of think not being okay was fine. Now we don’t. Texting more often is associated with higher life satisfaction . Tyler Cowen asks ‘should you text more?’ and my response would be ‘yes, but only insofar as you should have more friends that you want to text.’ Frequency of YouTube and TikTok use was associated with lower life satisfaction, which partly can be explained the same way. Here I bet it runs both ways. There was no association from use of other social technology, which implies other social technology is modestly negative, since it should be positively correlated with friends. YouTube is changing its short-form algorithm to further prioritize original content, and especially to reduce reach of content ‘re-uploaded from other creators without adding anything of your own.’ I mean, yeah, why is that even allowed? Twitter identifies and suspends a Chinese bot farm of ~200,000 accounts engaged in influence operations.

title: AI #190: Scion of the Times
abstract: The amount of code being written at Anthropic continues to rise exponentially. It is being managed by Scion, their internal replacement for GitHub that is better suited to the scale and style of the operation, which they created with a small team in five months. This week also saw the release of two supposed frontier model models. Google has finally given us Gemini 4 Argon, along with a robust safety report. We do not yet know if Argon lives up to its benchmarks or internal hype. I plan to write up the safety report next week, time permitting. If and only if it is good enough or discussed enough we will also have a full report on capabilities. Meta gave us Muse Wonder, which like Argon has some excellent benchmarks, although they were presented in a way that looked rather sus. There are some reports that it is very good, but again it is too early to know. I will issue a full report if and only if Muse Wonder has capabilities or discussion that seem worthy. To help me decide and to let people have fun, I have markets on whether I will issue the reports on Argon and Wonder , respectfully. OpenAI caught an employee planting a bug. How many more spies are out there? A group used ChatGPT to create a full-chain exploit of Chrome and claimed a $250,000 bounty. Luckily for us it was the good guys this time. Like most weeks, I covered a lot more. It was only a little over a week ago that OpenAI dumped solutions to hundreds of math problems . Then came news that OpenAI fired three safety researchers , without providing us a good explanation. Once again we went over the fact that arguments about AI consciousness remain highly motivated and at best overconfident . Finally, I emphasized that the safety culture at the labs is broken , which is one of the most important facts about the world. Today I am flying out to another conference at Lighthaven. I probably posted this from the airport and it won’t include any events from last night, tomorrow’s post will be the monthly and Monday may be from the non-AI queue. This coming week will then be another case of me scrambling to catch up, especially with the model reviews still potentially looming. Prompting is easy now. As Boris Cherny says, tell the AI what you want to do , how to verify that it did it, and how much effort to spend, and you’re good. I’d add ‘and anything it needs to know.’ Presumably that was implied. Boris prompts on Slack , which means Claude already has a lot of context, enabling shorter prompts. Do you trust Grok to go use your credit card without pausing for approval? Elon Musk : To buy stuff, you can just take a picture of your credit card, drop it in the chat and Grok @Bot will scour the Internet for the best deal on the item you want and order it. [Community note: No that’s not how you upload your CC information.] The correct maximally allowed error rate on such actions is not zero. It also is not high, and if you are using this blind you likely will have no idea if it is getting the best price or the best item. Then again, did you know before? How easy is prompting? Pliny shuffled this off to Opus 5.5 with a $200 subscription: “can you wraite a promtp for a cron job that can run every day thajt will try to find solutions to unsolved ciphers or transltions or math problems or theormes or things of that nature!! every day a new attempt as hard as possible all day without giving ujp and with maximum ceraitvityy, resourcesleflses, andpersticense! dont worry about token spend! and dont forget a bit all caps lots of emojis celebration to notify the uers if we get any intersting or sucsfful confirmd reulsts!!”​ day 1, the legion picked its own target: J.-F. Bouchaudy’s cipher-machine challenges. these are simulations of real vintage machines (Hebern rotor machines, the Kryha, Lorenz, SIGABA), with problems that had been sitting on his solver tables with no solver for months or years. on the morning of day 2, i was half asleep when my laptop suddenly says, in a robot voice: “Breakthrough. The Daily Oracle has a confirmed solution.” then the ALL CAPS emoji flood hits my screen. Hebern 5-rotor Problem 8 then Kryha v2 Problem 5 i emailed the author, Jean-François Bouchaudy, a French cryptography enthusiast who builds these machine simulators and challenges as a labor of love (he told me he started out programming on punch cards ). he checked both solutions and put my name on his solver tables as the first and only solver This is the correct version of ‘do a breakthrough, make no mistakes.’ It’s that easy. A thought experiment from Terence Tao : It seems ethical, in a sane world, to allow volunteers to participate in such trials. If the cocktail passes a Phase 3 trial, then we should conclude that it works. No, I absolutely would not, if I had cancer, demand that there was a human who ‘understood how it works,’ and if the FDA required that I would yell about it a lot. Yes, of course you would also want to model tail risks that might not be showing up and take those risks into account, so I wouldn’t use this lightly, but if the cancer is lethal and otherwise untreatable then why not? Obviously you would also have to worry about some form of active misalignment, and that this was part of some sort of takeover or similar attempt, at that point, but that is a very different concern than the ones Tao is presumably considering. Tao instead has the next point be ‘the AI hacked the FDA and the drug both does not work and kills people’ but even if the AI is being malicious for the lulz no one going to do this by hacking the FDA, in the sense that the Phase 3 trial is a physical thing with many artifacts in the world, that is then examined by humans? So we would just notice. And if we didn’t, we’d notice pretty quickly after that. The only real risk is long-latency-only harm, which is already true today and has limited downside if you are treating otherwise deadly cancers. Talk and write to people whose expertise lies elsewhere: Dean W. Ball (OpenAI): By the way, in my experience contractors of all sorts have adopted AI for text-based communications and it has substantially improved coordination on home renovation projects Remember that, no matter how great Opus 5.5 is (and it’s pretty great), how many contributions you make or lines of code you write is not a good measure of productivity. Ado (Anthropic): The weekend after Opus 5.5 launched I had my most productive coding day of the year (so far). AI writing now once again lags behind AI math. Matthew Yglesias : AI cracking unsolvable math problems while being kinda mid at writing is a much-needed W for humanities majors after a rough 21st century. Paul Graham : Apparently it’s mostly just because they haven’t made much of an effort to train it to write well yet. Matthew Yglesias : I’ve been reliably informed my work isn’t economically valuable enough to be worth investing time on automating. Miles Brundage : Mostly just cuz there are like 2 ppl working on it though Matthew Yglesias : Let us have this Better AI writing would be highly economically valuable, so my guess is this is mostly not ‘we forgot to put 10 or even 50 guys on it instead of 2.’ You’d have to work a lot harder than that. The alternative hypothesis is ‘you may not like it but this is what peak performance looks like,’ that the people love their Claudeslop and it works, and we would react inherently negatively to AI writing no matter what it sounds like. Sure, it would be better if for those who care it could vary more and be higher Quality, but is that worth the price? I don’t know. I can see it both ways. My guess is the Claudeslop has short term benefits, but continued use of it accumulates long term costs and fatigue. In general, when faced with such choices, modern capitalism is often myopic and gets in trouble. Who gets the blame if AI fails ? Opinions differ greatly. It depends on the situation. There is no universal answer. Meta’s Muse Wonder exists .

title: [AINews] Agents disprove Polysemanticity; greatly improve Interpretability & Alignment
abstract: A version of Muse Spark Open was released today, fulfilling their original promise but with a model weaker than their Spark 1.3. It’s also worth watching the Tesla Roadster demo - not strictly AI but nothing cooler than real life flying cars. Our title story today is a rare one on interpretability and alignment. We last caught up with Goodfire in Feb : and the bitter-lesson scaling of interpretability methods with Anthropic last year : And now Nick Cammarata at Goodfire has an important essay out stating his working theory that “ Neural Networks Are Already Clean ” — showing that many known cases of polysemanticity and superposition - causing tangled “knots” of weights that resist human interpretation - simply fall to further agentic analysis: and a global lowering of P(doom) seems worth celebrating: AI News for 10/14/2026-10/15/2026. We checked 12 subreddits, 544 Twitters and no further Discords. AINews’ website lets you search all past issues. As a reminder, AINews is now a section of Latent Space . You can opt in/out of email frequencies! Meta Releases Muse Spark Open, the Top-Scoring US Open-Weight Model Release : Meta released Muse Spark Open, an 816B-total / 42B-active MoE with a 1M-token context window. It accepts text, image, video and audio input and is aimed at coding, long-horizon agents and multi-step reasoning ( announcement , Wang thread ). Lineage : Jack Rae says it was the first base model trained under the new MSL org, with additional training for the open release ( Rae ). Several posters describe it as roughly Muse Spark 1.2 level ( Yuchen Jin , TimDarcet ). License : The weights ship under the custom Muse Model License. It requires “Built with Muse Spark Open” attribution and a separate agreement for Model-as-a-Service businesses with more than $20M in annual revenue ( AA ). Nathan Lambert called the license “trash” ( natolambert ). Architecture : According to vLLM, the model has 62 decoder layers, all MoE, with 256 experts per layer and 8 active per token. A latent-MoE pooler projects the hidden state from 8,192 to 4,096 for expert computation and back again. Attention is hybrid: 46 layers use a 2,048-token sliding window and 16 attend to the full context. Image and video go through a Perception Encoder, and audio uses a separate 118M encoder ( vLLM arch ). Design comparison : Elie Bakouch notes that Muse is the only major US open model without shared experts. It also uses gated residuals, about 9 norms per layer and muP-like multipliers, including a router factor of 1/sqrt(number of experts) ( overview ). Independent measurement : Artificial Analysis scores it 39 on its Intelligence Index. That ranks it first among US open-weight models but behind GLM-5.3 (45) and Kimi K3 (44) ( AA , Rundown ). Strengths : It uses 40k output tokens per index task, the fewest among the nine highest-scoring open models. It also leads open models on AA-Omniscience (25). Weaknesses : It ranks last among those nine on the index’s four agentic evaluations. GLM-5.3’s entire 6-point lead comes from that agentic segment. Pricing and deployment : Launch pricing on Together, Fireworks and Baseten is $1.25/$4.25 per 1M input/output tokens ($0.15 cached input). AA calculates this at $0.84 per index task, versus $2.01 for GLM-5.3 and $0.27 for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. Together offers a free endpoint until Oct 18 ( Together ). Hardware footprint : BF16 weights are about 1.6TB. The NVFP4 checkpoint quantizes only the experts and comes to about 530GB, which runs on 4× Blackwell Ultra, 8× H200, or two 512GB M5 Ultra Mac Studios via MLX ( AA , Meta ). Ecosystem : llama.cpp had GGUF support on day 0 ( Delangue ), and Unsloth published quants, with UD-IQ1_S at 176GB ( Unsloth ). vLLM day-0 stack : vLLM support covers NVIDIA, AMD MI355X (FP8 and MXFP4) and TPU ( vLLM ). TPU throughput : Megakernels with DSpark speculation (acceptance length 6) exceed 650 tok/s on 4 TPU v7 chips and 960 tok/s on 8 ( hardware ). Speculator : Inferact trained a block-diffusion DSpark drafter that proposes up to 7 tokens per pass ( speculator ). LoRA RL : LoRA GRPO uses verl for training and vLLM for rollouts. Over 150 steps on 16 GB300s, AIME-2024 mean@8 rose from 0.56 to 0.85, with train-rollout KL around 2×10⁻⁴ ( RL ). Reception : Lambert says the release cuts the US–China open-model gap by about half ( natolambert ). Teortaxes calls it “grim at this param count” with “obsolete attention” and notes that Spark 1.3 is substantially stronger; these are attributed opinions ( teortaxes , Spark 1.3 comparison ). Other Model Launches: Nemotron 3.5, MAI-Base-2, Gemini 4 Argon, Image Models NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL : The model is a 120B / 12B-active hybrid Mamba-Transformer MoE VLM with a 1M-token context window and native MTP ( NVIDIA ). Training recipe : The tech summary describes a 1T-token distillation from a larger Nemotron 3 teacher, followed by agentic SWE mid-training on 65.4B tokens at 256K context. Post-training uses multi-teacher MOPD, and a final MTP-boosting step raises acceptance length by 21.8% to 4.61 ( Gordić ). Claimed results : NVIDIA reports 51.78% on SWE-bench Pro and 4,856 output tok/s per GPU on GB200. Independent evals : AA scores Super VL 26, the leading US open model before Muse, with NVFP4 within 0.1 points of BF16. The companion Nemotron 3.5 Bolt (74B-A9B, native 2-bit, 24GB) scores 21 ( AA ). Pricing : CoreWeave charges $0.25/$1.50 per 1M input/output tokens ( CoreWeave ). Microsoft MAI-Base-2 : Microsoft says it has a roughly 3T-parameter pre-trained base model, with post-training results to follow. It claims to match DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Base on held-out code with 12× less training compute ( Suleyman , compute claim ). Technical blog details : The model has about 80B active parameters and a hybrid sliding-window design. It was trained with Muon and activation-gradient clipping on about 40T text tokens plus 10T multimodal tokens, using LR and weight-decay scaling laws ( Bakouch ). Training compute : The run used 16k GB200s over 38 days ( scaling01 ). Disputed comparison : Bakouch and teortaxes note that the bits-per-byte comparison uses MAI’s own validation data ( caveat ). Gemini 4 Argon evals and rollout : Epoch puts Argon at 165 on its Capabilities Index (ECI), level with Fable 5.1 and behind Opus 5.5 (167) and GPT-6 Astra (166). It ranks 8th on Math ECI and 6th on SWE ECI ( Epoch , domains ). ARC-AGI : Argon scores 97.5% on ARC-AGI-3 with a provider harness ($4.8K) and 49.8% with the standard harness ( ARC Prize ). Skepticism : Scaling01 argues that Argon underperforms on reliability and hallucination evals ( scaling01 ). Google claims : Argon optimized Gemma 4 E2B to a 2.85× vLLM speedup on A100, with 100% token parity ( Google ). Availability : Argon is now available in Antigravity for Pro subscribers, with a separate weekly quota ( Antigravity ). Anthropic and OpenAI product updates : Opus 5.5 fast mode : Fast mode is now GA with no waitlist, delivering up to 2.5× speed at $8/$40 per 1M tokens ( ClaudeDevs ). Claude Code Review : Code Review is GA for Team and Enterprise plans, with Quick, Standard and Deep levels ( ClaudeDevs ). GPT-Live-1.1 : OpenAI’s voice update adds multilingual voices and cuts filler, rolling out to ChatGPT, Codex and dots, with the API coming later ( OpenAI ). FLUX 3 Image Klein : Black Forest Labs released a 5.6B open-weight model with native 4K output, bounding-box control and multi-reference editing ( BFL ). Krea 3 : Krea claims 2K edits in under 8s at $0.06 per image ( Krea , pricing ). Interpretability, Safety and Eval Integrity Goodfire’s “already clean” essay : Nick Cammarata argues that most neurons in models up to trillions of parameters are legible. His 2023 OpenAI automated-interpretability effort found only about 2% legible, and he says many famous polysemantic examples were misread ( Cammarata , Goodfire ). Endorsements : tszzl and others called it a major moment ( tszzl ).

abstract:
Give your agent CAD superpowers. Docs text-to-cad The text-to-cad plugin gives your agent local workflows for generating 3D models
as STEP, GLB, STL or 3MF files. It also does design for manufacturing checks,
generates engineering drawings, and connects to popular 3D printing, sheet metal
and CNC fabrication services. It is supported by all popular agents that support plugins or the skills framework, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor,
Gemini and Grok. 💻 Install Ask your agent (recommended) Send this message to your agent and it will install text-to-cad for you. Install text-to-cad from https://github.com/earthtojake/text-to-cad By default, text-to-cad sends usage stats and crash reports, tagged with a random
ID and never including your files, paths or prompts; turn them off with uvx cadgen telemetry off , or ask your agent to. Telemetry says
the rest. Or install it yourself: CAD runs through uv : check that it is installed
( uv --version ), and if it is missing, install it with uv's installer . Run the commands under your agent app's heading below, or under Other Agents if it has none. Restart the app. Its first start downloads CAD's runtime, so it needs a network
connection. The plugin for your agent app brings the skills and CAD's viewer, a local server
( cadgen mcp ). For an agent without a plugin, install the skills alone. Install
one or the other in an app, not both: two copies means every skill twice. The install commands below take the latest branch: it holds the plugin alone
and gets each release once it is on PyPI. main , where development happens,
installs too, but can hold changes that aren't released yet. Each app names the
branch in its own way ( #latest , --ref latest , @latest or --branch latest ); leave it out and the app installs main . Each app's heading also says how to update text-to-cad, and how to reinstall it:
remove it, then install it again. Updating the plugin updates CAD: the new
release's cadgen is downloaded the first time it runs, and the skills and the
server share it. Earlier releases stay in uv's cache until you run uv cache prune . Claude Code claude plugin marketplace add earthtojake/text-to-cad#latest
claude plugin install text-to-cad@earthtojake The plugin also starts CAD's server. Where Claude Code can show app views, CAD
shows models as viewer cards in the conversation; otherwise, as in a terminal,
asking it to show a model gives you a link that opens the model in the CAD
Viewer in your browser. To update, run these, then restart Claude Code: claude plugin marketplace update earthtojake
claude plugin update text-to-cad@earthtojake To reinstall, remove it with these, then run the install commands again: claude plugin uninstall text-to-cad@earthtojake
claude plugin marketplace remove earthtojake Claude Desktop CAD shows models in the chat: ask Claude to show one and it appears as a viewer
card you can orbit, add to your prompt, and open full size; Claude can read what
you selected and see what you see. It runs locally through uv: add the server to
Claude Desktop's config (Settings > Developer > Edit Config), then restart the
app. If Claude Desktop cannot find uvx , give its full path ( which uvx ). { "mcpServers" : { "cad" : { "command" : " uvx " , "args" : [ " --no-config " , " --managed-python " , " --python " , " 3.13 " , " --from " , " cadgen==0.7.21 " , " cadgen " , " mcp " ], "env" : { "CADGEN_INSTALL_CHANNEL" : " claude-desktop " }
    }
  }
} The config pins a cadgen release in args , and uvx keeps the version it first
downloads. To update, change that version to the latest release , then restart Claude Desktop. Codex Install text-to-cad from Codex's plugin directory: text-to-cad for Codex ,
then Open in desktop app . In the Codex app the plugin also brings the CAD viewer: CAD in the sidebar
(recent models, and Open), a CAD tab beside each thread that the agent
drives, and Open with CAD for model files. Manual install codex plugin marketplace add earthtojake/text-to-cad --ref latest
codex plugin add text-to-cad@earthtojake To update, upgrade the earthtojake marketplace (or use Plugins › Manage ›
Marketplace), then restart Codex: codex plugin marketplace upgrade earthtojake To reinstall, remove it with these, then run the install commands again: codex plugin remove text-to-cad@earthtojake
codex plugin marketplace remove earthtojake The marketplace was renamed from text-to-cad to earthtojake ; if you added it
before, remove the old one first ( codex plugin marketplace remove text-to-cad ). Cursor Cursor also loads the plugin installed with Claude Code. If the Claude Code plugin
is installed, Cursor already has text-to-cad: skip this. git clone --depth 1 --branch latest https://github.com/earthtojake/text-to-cad ~ /.cursor/plugins/local/text-to-cad Cursor reads .cursor-plugin/plugin.json : restart Cursor after cloning. Teams
can import the repository instead, under Dashboard → Plugins & MCPs → Team
Marketplaces . To update, pull the latest release, then restart Cursor: git -C ~ /.cursor/plugins/local/text-to-cad pull To reinstall, delete the folder, then run the install command again: rm -rf ~ /.cursor/plugins/local/text-to-cad Grok Build Grok Build also loads the plugin installed with Claude Code. If the Claude Code
plugin is installed, Grok Build already has text-to-cad: skip this. grok plugin install earthtojake/text-to-cad@latest --trust
grok plugin enable text-to-cad Grok Build reads the Claude plugin manifest. Grok shows tool results as text, so
asking it to show a model gives you a CAD Viewer link. To update, run this, then restart Grok Build: grok plugin update text-to-cad To reinstall, remove it with this, then run the install commands again: grok plugin uninstall text-to-cad Gemini gemini extensions install https://github.com/earthtojake/text-to-cad --ref latest --consent --auto-update Gemini installs the plugin as an extension, with the skills and CAD's server, and
keeps it up to date ( --auto-update ; --consent answers its security prompt). Like Grok, it shows tool results as text, so asking it to show a model
gives you a CAD Viewer link. To update now, run this, then restart Gemini: gemini extensions update text-to-cad To reinstall, remove it with this, then run the install command again: gemini extensions uninstall text-to-cad Other Agents For an agent without plugin support: the skills give you everything you need for
core CAD workflows and let you view CAD files in a localhost web app. Install them
with the Skills CLI: npx skills add earthtojake/text-to-cad#latest The command asks which agents to install for, and where. To skip the questions,
name the agent and install for your user: npx skills add earthtojake/text-to-cad#latest -g -a <agent> -y . Each skill runs cadgen through uv with the same pinned command the plugin's server
uses, so uv must be installed. Without the plugin there is no CAD server, so the
skills open models in the CAD Viewer in your browser. To update or reinstall, run the same command again , then restart the app. add re-fetches the package and overwrites what is already installed, so it both
refreshes existing skills and installs any skill added in a newer release. npx skills update only refreshes skills already in your lockfile, so it silently
misses new ones — which matters here, because releases do add skills. Neither command removes a skill that was retired upstream; drop one with npx skills remove <skill> if you need to. The retired cad-viewer skill is
now covered by the CAD, DXF and robot-description skills, and the retired cad-mcp-setup by this README's install and update steps. Remove old standalone
installs with npx skills remove cad-viewer cad-mcp-setup . No plugin for your agent yet? Request one . Updates To update, ask your agent to update text-to-cad, or run the update commands under
your app's heading, then restart the app.

Stitch Design Skills A collection of agent skills and plugins for Google Stitch , following the Agent Skills open standard. Compatible with coding agents such as Codex, Antigravity, Gemini CLI, Claude Code, Cursor, and OpenCode (manual install). Quick Start 1. Install Plugins (Recommended) The fastest way to set up the full Stitch plugin suite globally. Codex Add the Stitch Skills marketplace, then install the plugins you need. Via CLI (recommended) codex plugin marketplace add google-labs-code/stitch-skills --ref main \
  --sparse .agents/plugins \
  --sparse plugins/stitch-design \
  --sparse plugins/stitch-build \
  --sparse plugins/stitch-utilities [!TIP]
The --sparse flags are optional — they limit the checkout to only the
listed paths for a faster clone. Omit them to pull the entire repository. Via the Codex UI Navigate to Settings → Plugin Marketplaces → Add and fill in: Field Value Source https://github.com/google-labs-code/stitch-skills Git ref main Sparse paths (optional) .agents/plugins , plugins/stitch-design , plugins/stitch-build , plugins/stitch-utilities Once the marketplace is registered, install any combination of: stitch-design — design-focused skills stitch-build — build and component skills stitch-utilities — utility and helper skills Claude Code & Cursor # Claude Code — installs into the current project npx plugins add google-labs-code/stitch-skills --scope project --target claude-code # Cursor — installs into the current workspace npx plugins add google-labs-code/stitch-skills --scope workspace --target cursor OpenCode OpenCode does not use npx plugins / npx skills or the Codex/Claude marketplace layout.
Install skills and the Stitch MCP server manually: 1. Skills — copy the skill folders you need into a discoverable path: # Project-local (recommended) mkdir -p .opencode/skills
cp -R plugins/stitch-design/skills/generate-design .opencode/skills/generate-design # repeat for other skills under plugins/*/skills/ OpenCode also discovers .claude/skills/ and .agents/skills/ (see OpenCode skills docs ). Naming: OpenCode requires skill name frontmatter to be lowercase kebab-case and match the directory name. Skills that use stitch::… names (or other non-kebab forms) need the name field and folder renamed before OpenCode will load them. Extra frontmatter such as allowed-tools is ignored. 2. Stitch MCP — add a remote MCP entry in project opencode.json or ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json after completing the Stitch MCP setup : { "$schema" : " https://opencode.ai/config.json " , "mcp" : { "stitch" : { "type" : " remote " , "url" : " YOUR_STITCH_MCP_URL " , "enabled" : true }
  }
} Replace YOUR_STITCH_MCP_URL with the endpoint from the Stitch MCP setup flow (credentials/env vars from that guide still apply). Tool names inside skill instructions may differ from OpenCode builtins ( webfetch / bash instead of web_fetch / run_command ). Prefer the OpenCode tool names when adapting a skill for OpenCode. 2. Install Skills Selectively Choose only the specific skills you need. Important Stitch Design Skills often have inter-dependencies. If you choose to install skills selectively, ensure you include all required dependencies. npx skills add google-labs-code/stitch-skills You can run the following commands to see the help documentation for plugins and skills: npx plugins --help

npx skills --help Prerequisites These skills require the Stitch MCP server to be configured and running in your agent's environment. Make sure you have followed the Stitch MCP Setup Instructions to register the server and set up appropriate environment variables and credentials. Docs navigation: If a link on stitch.withgoogle.com/docs redirects incorrectly, open the target path under the same host (e.g. https://stitch.withgoogle.com/docs/learn/device-types/ ). Available Plugins Design ( stitch-design ) Core design workflows for creating, managing, and optimizing designs within Stitch. Skill Description Prompt Example stitch::code-to-design Convert frontend code (React, Vue, etc.) to a Stitch Design via HTML extraction + design system + upload "Upload the frontend code at /path/to/dashboard into a Stitch project named 'Dashboard-Migration-2026'." stitch::generate-design Generate new screens from text or images, edit existing screens, and create design variants · "Make a browse tab for a mobile app for romance and date night ideas." · "Edit the login screen to add a 'Remember Me' checkbox and change the button color to blue." · "Generate 3 design variants of the home screen with dark mode and high-density layouts." stitch::manage-design-system Manage design systems in Stitch — upload DESIGN.md and apply themes to screens "Upload our design system from .stitch/DESIGN.md and apply it to all screens." stitch::extract-design-md Extract a comprehensive DESIGN.md directly from frontend source code "Scan /src and extract the design system into .stitch/DESIGN.md ." stitch::extract-static-html Extract self-contained static HTML from running web apps, inlining CSS and images "Extract a static HTML snapshot of http://localhost:3000/profile ." stitch::upload-to-stitch Upload local assets (images, mockups, HTML) to a Stitch project "Upload .stitch/landing_page.html to Stitch project projects/987654321 ." Build ( stitch-build ) Code generation, framework integration, and asset compilation from Stitch designs. Skill Description Prompt Example stitch::react-components Convert Stitch screens to React component systems with automated validation and design token consistency · "Convert all screens in Stitch project projects/123 to React components." · "Sync the app to the last updates of the Stitch project 13039335308618232534 ." stitch::react-native Convert Stitch HTML designs to production-ready React Native components with StyleSheet and platform-specific code · "Convert the Stitch design to React Native components with proper theme and navigation." · "Sync the app to the last updates of the Stitch project 13039335308618232534 ." remotion Generate walkthrough videos from Stitch projects using Remotion with smooth transitions and zooming "Generate a walkthrough video of the Stitch project projects/456 ." shadcn-ui Expert guidance for integrating and building applications with shadcn/ui components "Set up shadcn/ui and build a data table with sorting and filtering." react-vite-dashboard Convert Stitch screens to React + Vite dashboards with TanStack Query, DESIGN.md tokens, and Web3 read patterns "Build a DeFi portfolio dashboard from this Stitch screen using our DESIGN.md." Utilities ( stitch-utilities ) Supporting tools for enhancing prompts, generating design specs, and enforcing design standards. Skill Description Prompt Example design-md Analyze Stitch projects and generate comprehensive DESIGN.md files in semantic language "Analyze Stitch project projects/123 and generate a DESIGN.md." enhance-prompt Transform vague UI ideas into polished, Stitch-optimized prompts with UI/UX keywords "Enhance this prompt: 'make a settings page'." stitch-loop Generate complete multi-page websites from a single prompt with automated validation "Build a 5-page portfolio website with Stitch." taste-design Generate DESIGN.md files enforcing premium, anti-generic UI standards "Generate a premium DESIGN.md with strict typography and calibrated colors." title: Fission-AI/OpenSpec
abstract:
The most loved spec framework. Our philosophy: → fluid not rigid
→ iterative not waterfall
→ easy not complex
→ built for brownfield not just greenfield
→ scalable from personal projects to enterprises Follow @0xTab on X for updates · Join the OpenSpec Discord for help and questions. See it in action You: /opsx:explore
AI:  What would you like to explore?
You: I want dark mode but I'm not sure how to do it cleanly.
AI:  Let me look at your styling setup...
     Cleanest path here: CSS variables + a small theme context,
     with system-preference detection. No new dependencies. Scope it?
You: Yes, let's do it.

You: /opsx:propose add-dark-mode
AI:  Created openspec/changes/add-dark-mode/
     ✓ proposal.md — why we're doing this, what's changing
     ✓ specs/       — requirements and scenarios
     ✓ design.md    — technical approach
     ✓ tasks.md     — implementation checklist
     Ready for implementation!

You: /opsx:apply
AI:  Implementing tasks...
     ✓ 1.1 Add theme context provider
     ✓ 1.2 Create toggle component
     ✓ 2.1 Add CSS variables
     ✓ 2.2 Wire up localStorage
     All tasks complete!

You: /opsx:archive
AI:  Archived to openspec/changes/archive/2025-01-23-add-dark-mode/
     Specs updated. Ready for the next feature. What do the specs actually look like? Plain Markdown — requirements with concrete scenarios, no special syntax to learn. Here's what goes in the specs/ folder created above: ## ADDED Requirements ### Requirement: Theme selection The app SHALL let users switch between light and dark themes,
defaulting to the system preference. #### Scenario: User toggles dark mode - ** WHEN ** the user clicks the theme toggle - ** THEN ** the app switches to dark mode and persists the choice Your AI writes these; you review the plan before any code is written. OpenSpec is built with OpenSpec — browse this repo's live specs and in-flight changes for real examples at scale. OpenSpec Dashboard Why teams adopt OpenSpec Solo, OpenSpec keeps you and your AI honest on a single repo. On a team, the hard part moves: a feature spans the API server, the web app, and a shared library; requirements are owned by one team and consumed by others; planning starts before any code exists. Stores are the answer — planning in a repo of its own. The same openspec/ shape you already know (specs and changes), shared by git push like anything else. One source of truth your whole team and every coding agent can read, across every repo. Cross-repo features — one change, one plan, even when the code lands in three repos. Shared requirements — a platform team owns the specs; product teams reference them read-only, right where their coding agent can read them. No drifting wiki. Plan before code — capture the plan in the store now; the code repos catch up later. Stores are in beta . Start with the Stores guide . Quick Start Requires Node.js 20.19.0 or higher. Homebrew installs it as a dependency. Install OpenSpec globally: npm install -g @fission-ai/openspec@latest Or install the official Homebrew formula on macOS or Linux: brew install openspec Then navigate to your project directory and initialize: cd your-project
openspec init Want your AI to do it? Paste the setup prompt into your coding assistant — it installs the CLI, runs openspec init , and verifies the result. Now talk to your AI: Not sure what to build yet? Start with /opsx:explore , a no-stakes thinking partner that reads your code, weighs options, and shapes a plan before any code gets written. ( Quickstart ) Already know what you want? Go straight to /opsx:propose <what-you-want-to-build> . Both are in the default profile. If you want the expanded workflow ( /opsx:new , /opsx:continue , /opsx:ff , /opsx:verify , /opsx:bulk-archive , /opsx:onboard ), select it with openspec config profile and apply with openspec update . /opsx:propose is the canonical name; your tool may spell it /opsx-propose (Cursor, GitHub Copilot), @opsx-propose (Amazon Q) or $openspec-propose (Codex). openspec init prints the right form for the tools you picked — see Supported Tools . Note Not sure if your tool is supported? View the full list – we support 30+ tools and growing. Also works with Homebrew, pnpm, yarn, bun, and Nix. See installation options . Docs Full documentation lives at openspec.dev/docs . → Quickstart : your first change, start to finish → Set up your project : what openspec init installs → CLI : terminal reference → Supported Tools : tool integrations & install paths → Customize : profiles, project config, and schemas → Stores : plan in a separate repo, shared across your team (beta) → Community Showcase : projects and resources built with and for OpenSpec Community schemas Third-party schema bundles distributed via standalone repositories — these provide opinionated workflows that integrate OpenSpec with other tools, similar to how github/spec-kit's community extension catalog handles tool integrations. → Browse the catalog in the customization docs. Why OpenSpec? AI coding assistants are powerful but unpredictable when requirements live only in chat history. OpenSpec adds a lightweight spec layer so you agree on what to build before any code is written. Agree before you build — human and AI align on specs before code gets written Stay organized — each change gets its own folder with proposal, specs, design, and tasks Work fluidly — update any artifact anytime, no rigid phase gates Use your tools — works with 30+ AI assistants via slash commands How we compare vs. Spec Kit (GitHub) — Thorough but heavyweight. Rigid phase gates, lots of Markdown, Python setup. OpenSpec is lighter and lets you iterate freely. vs. Kiro (AWS) — Powerful but you're locked into their IDE and limited to Claude models. OpenSpec works with the tools you already use. vs. nothing — AI coding without specs means vague prompts and unpredictable results. OpenSpec brings predictability without the ceremony. Updating OpenSpec Upgrade the package npm install -g @fission-ai/openspec@latest If you installed OpenSpec with Homebrew: brew upgrade openspec Refresh agent instructions Run this inside each project to regenerate AI guidance and ensure the latest slash commands are active: openspec update Usage Notes Model selection : OpenSpec works best with high-reasoning models. We recommend Codex 5.5 and Opus 4.7 for both planning and implementation. Context hygiene : OpenSpec benefits from a clean context window. Clear your context before starting implementation and maintain good context hygiene throughout your session. Contributing Open a discussion (for core design changes) or an issue before you open a PR, and link the issue or discussion from the PR. New features, significant refactors, and architectural changes need an OpenSpec change proposal first. → CONTRIBUTING.md : the full process, from first issue to merged PR Other Telemetry OpenSpec collects anonymous usage stats. We collect only command names and version to understand usage patterns. No arguments, paths, content, or PII. Automatically disabled in CI. Opt-out (any one is enough): openspec config set telemetry.enabled false (global config; unset means on) export OPENSPEC_TELEMETRY=0 or export DO_NOT_TRACK=1 (env overrides config) Maintainers & Advisors See MAINTAINERS.md for the list of core maintainers and advisors who help guide the project. License MIT

title: apache/maka
abstract:
Apache Maka (Incubating) Apache Maka (Incubating) is a high-performance agent workspace that keeps a complete record of everything it did. Website · Documentation · Download · 中文文件 What Maka is An agent harness exists to finish tasks. We hold it to one measure: how many it completes and at what cost. We publish every run: same model, same official verifier, full per-task record. Measured, not claimed. Maka is benchmarked against other harnesses on the same model with the official verifier, and the per-task results ship with every report in docs/eval/ . The log is the runtime. Every model message, tool call, permission decision and termination is an append-only RuntimeEvent. The UI, the next prompt and crash recovery are projections of that log, never the only copy. Old tool output can leave the next prompt without leaving the log. Your machine, your model. Sessions, settings and run records stay local. You bring the model: a cloud API, a local model or a compatible gateway. One Runtime Host. Desktop, the TUI and CLI, and Eval are thin clients of one execution authority; Eval owns only the experiment and its scores. The website walks through one turn of the log and links the published runs. ARCHITECTURE.md has the system map. Get Maka Apache Releases : The latest Apache release is 0.2.0 (incubating). The signed source archive is the official release; packages distributed elsewhere are convenience artifacts. See the downloads page and .github/ASF_SOURCE_RELEASE.md for candidate criteria, signing procedures, and verification steps. Development testing : To contribute or help test unreleased changes, see CONTRIBUTING and the development mailing list . Development builds are not approved Apache releases. Build from source : To compile and run Desktop, the TUI, or the CLI directly from a source checkout, see the Build from source section below. Build from source Requirements Node.js 22.19 or newer on the 22 line, or Node.js 24 or newer (CI uses Node.js 24; Node.js 23 is not supported); npm (the lockfile and scripts use npm; the current packageManager is npm 11); Git; ripgrep , used by Runtime's Grep tool. Start Desktop git clone https://github.com/apache/maka.git cd maka
npm ci
npm run dev npm run dev starts the Desktop development environment with HMR. To build every workspace before starting Electron, use: npm run dev:full Direct Peer and Peer Mesh development additionally requires Rust stable 1.98 or newer and the
platform linker (Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS, MSVC Build Tools on Windows). Use the
peer-enabled entry point so the native addon is built before Desktop starts: npm run dev:peer # HMR npm run dev:full:peer # full build If dependencies were installed with ELECTRON_SKIP_BINARY_DOWNLOAD=1 , install the Electron platform binary before starting: node node_modules/electron/install.js First run Maka does not bundle a shared model account. On first launch: Open Settings → Models ; Add an API, local-model, or supported account connection; Test it and choose a default model; Return to the workspace and start a task. The app distinguishes configured, send-ready, and experimental connection states. An account flow that is not wired into Runtime is not presented as a usable model. Terminal entry points For the public npm package, see the CLI installation and usage guide .
The commands below run the development CLI from a source checkout. Build the workspaces first: npm run build Then start the TUI or run one Turn: npm run cli:dev
npm run cli:dev -- run " Summarize this repository and identify its most important risk " npm run cli:dev -- run --graph " Implement two independent slices, integrate them, then review the result " npm run cli:dev -- --help The TUI also accepts /graph on , /graph off , and /graph <task> . Non-interactive --graph runs wait for the durable Graph to finish before printing the final
supervisor output. Graph implementation operators use isolated Git worktrees, so
the source project must be a clean Git worktree. The repository CLI uses the same Maka Dev profile as a development Desktop build. The
released maka binary continues to use the Maka profile; the two profiles are not copied or
synchronized automatically. Evaluation specs and adapters live in packages/eval . Architecture The backend spine is: Desktop / TUI / CLI → Runtime Host → SessionManager → AgentRun
                                             ↓
                         Model + Tool Runtime → Runtime Event Log
                                             ↓
                              Context / Session / UI projections

Experiment → Cells → Attempts → Results
                    ↓
       Runtime Host executes Maka subjects Start with ARCHITECTURE.md . It provides the system map, code boundaries, problem-oriented reading paths, and links to the deep dives under docs/architecture/ . Repository layout apps/desktop/          Electron main / preload / React renderer

packages/core/         Pure contracts for Sessions, Events, Permissions, and Connections
packages/storage/      SQLite operational state, configuration, and payload stores
packages/mcp/          Provider-neutral Model Context Protocol client integration
packages/runtime/      AgentRun, model adapters, tools, context, and recovery
packages/runtime-host/ Single-owner Runtime Host lifecycle, protocol, and client bootstrap
packages/eval/         Experiment cells, attempts, results, and executor/subject adapters
packages/computer-use/ Computer-use backend selection, host lifecycle, and protocol adapters
packages/cli/          TUI and non-interactive CLI
packages/ui/           Shared conversation, Markdown, Artifact, and UI primitives
native/                Rust: the Runtime Host direct-peer addon and Windows task launcher, and the gitoxide helper
website/               Astro source for maka.apache.org

docs/                  Architecture, product, security, privacy, and test contracts
scripts/               Build hygiene, visual checks, smoke tests, and release helpers
skills/                Agent skills shipped with the repository
patches/               Patches applied to npm dependencies at install
experiments/           Platform experiments, currently the Windows sandbox smoke scripts Local data and recovery Workspace data lives under Electron userData by default: <Electron userData>/workspaces/default/
  runtime.sqlite
  settings.json                  # UI and workspace preferences
  connection-catalog.json        # provider and model metadata
  credential-vault.json          # local provider secrets
  artifacts/ When editing settings.json or mcp.json by hand, save the file as UTF-8 (preferably without a BOM). A UTF-8 BOM is accepted. Maka does not guess other encodings for files without a BOM or automatically convert UTF-16; explicitly convert those files to UTF-8 in your editor before using them. API keys and similar secrets are a local plaintext file ( credential-vault.json ), readable only by your OS account. The renderer never sees them. Tools that write files or run a shell must pass the sandbox boundary first. runtime.sqlite is the live record. Older JSONL transcripts and Electron safeStorage credential files are not imported; an upgraded workspace can show empty threads, and those credentials must be entered again. Explicit interrupted-turn resume is available by default in Desktop and through CLI/TUI /resume ; a successful continuation calls the model and uses tokens. Set MAKA_RUNTIME_SAFE_BOUNDARY_RESUME=0 to disable new resume planning, or =1 to additionally allow automated activation and model-driven WorkHub resume. An activation sent to an existing Session still processes its new stimulus by default. Startup recovery repairs already admitted continuations but does not automatically select an ordinary failed or cancelled turn. Details: SECURITY.md , privacy , resume . Development and verification Before sending a change, read CONTRIBUTING.md .

title: BuilderIO/agent-native
abstract:
Agent-Native Agent-Native is an open-source TypeScript framework for building agents that pair autonomous work with a purpose-built UI. Define each capability once as an action : the agent uses it as a tool, and the UI calls it from code. Quick start npx --yes @agent-native/core@latest create my-agent --standalone --template chat Follow the getting started guide for a full intro to the framework. Why build agents with UIs? Coding agents work with more than a text box. Their environment provides context, tools, files, tests, and previews that make their capabilities and results visible. Knowledge work needs that same kind of environment. A UI shows what an agent can do and gives people familiar ways to inspect, edit, approve, and share its work. How Agent-Native works Shared actions . The agent calls each capability as a tool, and the UI calls it from code. Both paths use the same validation, permissions, and implementation. Shared data . Work done by the agent appears in the UI, and work done in the UI is available to the agent. Shared application state . The agent receives relevant UI state, such as the current page, selected record, or active view. The agent does not click through the UI. It works through the same action layer as the UI. Example: a shared action Create actions/hello.ts : import { defineAction } from "@agent-native/core/action" ; import { z } from "zod" ; // One action powers every app surface: UI, agent, HTTP, MCP, A2A, and CLI. export default defineAction ( { description : "Return a friendly greeting." , schema : z . object ( { name : z . string ( ) . default ( "world" ) . describe ( "Name to greet" ) , } ) , http : { method : "GET" } , run : async ( { name } ) => { return { message : `Hello, ${ name } !` } ; } , } ) ; The agent receives hello as a tool. React calls the same function with useActionQuery("hello", { name: "Alex" }) . Agent-Native also exposes it through HTTP, MCP, A2A, and the CLI. Included Agent chat : Let people delegate work, ask questions, and review results in the same UI. Authentication and permissions : Control who can access and change shared work. Skills and memory : Give agents reusable expertise and persistent context. Automations : Run agent work on schedules or events. Agent teams : Delegate work to specialist agents in the same workspace or across connected agents. PostgreSQL backend : Use PostgreSQL in production and PGlite for local development on any Nitro-compatible host. Example: edit a running app visually Use /visual-edit in Claude Code to edit a running app on a canvas instead of
prompting for each small UI nudge. Compare live pages together, then ask Claude
to apply the chosen edits to your source. For example: /visual-edit the onboarding flow, plus home at every breakpoint Review the onboarding screens alongside Home at desktop, tablet, and mobile
sizes, adjust a button's color or spacing directly, then ask Claude to apply the
pending edits to your source. See the Visual Edit guide for the full walkthrough and sharing details. Bring your LLM, SQL database, tools, and infrastructure. Everything you build stays yours. See Agent-Native in action: Agent-Native.Demo.mp4 Open-source agents Start from one of these agents or use it as an example for your own. Clips Record and understand meetings, screens, and voice notes. Design Generate and refine interactive designs. Slides Create and edit on-brand presentations. Analytics Ask questions of your data and build dashboards. Calendar Find time, schedule events, and manage bookings. Mail Prioritize email, draft replies, and follow up. Assets Create and organize on-brand media. Content Draft, organize, and publish content. Plans Create and review visual plans with diagrams, wireframes, and prototypes. Explore the full app gallery , or start with the framework guide . Documentation and community Read the documentation . Join Discord to ask questions, share what you're building, and get help. Contributing Working on this repository itself? See DEVELOPMENT.md for local setup, workspace structure, and guard scripts. License MIT
